subject: Enterprise access controls kickoff: SSO/SCIM + service accounts for TruBank

Subject: Enterprise access controls kickoff: SSO/SCIM + service accounts for TruBank

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your inference platform. To keep the onboarding P0 focused, this thread will track the access controls work (SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, IP allowlists, and service accounts). Attached: a mutual action plan and a SCIM mapping template to speed validation.

Initial asks from our side:
- IdP metadata (XML or metadata URL) for SAML; preferred NameID format and primary email attribute.
- SCIM service account: please confirm the team that will create the scoped token and where we should send token provisioning instructions.
- IP allowlist ranges for your staging and prod egress (we’ll need CIDR blocks).
- Any org-level policies needing special handling (session timeout shorter than default, device trust, legacy SSO restrictions).

Quick notes on Redwood defaults (we can adjust per your security policy):
- SAML: ACS URL: https://api.redwood.ai/sso/acs/TRB-4821; Entity ID: urn:redwood:trubank:TRB-4821
- SCIM: token-based provisioning with scim:read + scim:write scopes (we recommend scim:write for provisioning; tokens rotate every 90 days)
- Service accounts: scoped to tenant only; recommend naming pattern redwood-scim-TRB-staging / redwood-scim-TRB-prod
- IP allowlisting: we support per-tenant CIDR ranges and can do staged roll (staging first).

Can you share IdP metadata and a staging CIDR range this week? We’re aiming to run an end-to-end staging provisioning on May 12.

Attaching: mutual_action_plan_trubank.xlsx and redwood_scim_mapping_template.csv

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

- Service account privileges: we need clarity on the least privilege required — which SCIM scopes are truly necessary for initial provisioning?
- Org policies: we currently enforce 8-hour session timeout for admin consoles and require device MFA for admin roles. Can Redwood accommodate shorter session TTLs for elevated roles?

We’d like to run the staged run on May 12 in the AM (ET). Please confirm if that works.

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the Okta metadata link. A few implementation items and recommendations from CS/Onboarding:

SAML configuration (recommended):
- AssertionConsumerService (ACS): https://api.redwood.ai/sso/acs/TRB-4821
- Entity ID: urn:redwood:trubank:TRB-4821
- NameID format: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress
- Required attributes: email (primary), given_name, family_name, groups (optional)
- Signature/Encrypt: we recommend signed assertions; encryption optional if you enforce TLS at the load balancer

SCIM provisioning notes:
- We attached redwood_scim_mapping_template.csv. Minimal attributes for first-pass provisioning: userName (email), active (true/false), givenName, familyName, externalId (bank employee id), groups (for RBAC mapping).
- Group push: enable for the staging run only if you want group-backed RBAC. Otherwise we recommend a limited subset for P0 (admins + service users).

Service accounts & scoping:
- Suggested naming: redwood-scim-trubank-staging and redwood-scim-trubank-prod.
- Scope: scim:read and scim:write for staging token; production token we can issue with scim:write only plus a restricted list of groups.
- Token rotation: recommended 90 days; we can integrate with your Vault if you prefer (Doc link attached).

Session & org policies:
- We can honor an 8-hour session TTL for the Redwood Console sessions tied to your SSO. For admin elevation we support conditional step-up MFA via the IdP.
- Device trust: we can require device posture checks for specific admin roles, but we’ll need a mapping table of roles to enforcement (attach in Drive).

Next steps:
1) Can you share the staging IdP metadata file (or confirm Okta link works) — looks good from our side.
2) Confirm whether you want group push enabled in staging.
3) Confirm a 2-hour maintenance window on May 12 09:00–11:00 ET for IP allowlist change and provisioning test.

I’ve attached the SCIM mapping template and a short checklist for SAML validation. Jonas — can you confirm the ACS entity on our infra side before we lock the slot?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Dylan —

Quick answers inline:
- Session TTL: Redwood defaults to 12 hours for console sessions keyed to SSO assertions; we can honor 8 hours for your tenant — we’ll apply that after the staging run.
- Token rotation TTL: recommended 90 days; we can sync with your Vault for automated rotation if you provide API access.
- Runbook for May 12 (short):
  1) 09:00 ET — validate Okta metadata and SAML assertion (Jonas + Dylan)
  2) 09:20 ET — provision SCIM token to staging (TruBank infra) and run user push (Jonas observes)
  3) 09:45 ET — validate users and groups in staging; run sample auth flows
  4) 10:15 ET — IP allowlist change to add staging CIDR for Redwood egress (TruBank infra)
  5) 10:40 ET — rollback plan if >30% failure: remove allowlist entry and revert provisioning with our CS script
  6) 10:55 ET — acceptance: successful SAML login + 10 sample users provisioned and group mappings intact

I’ll upload the short runbook to the shared link and we’ll add run participants.

See you on the 12th — thanks for the speedy coordination.

Jonas
